layouts.rooms: Rooms and halls on a grid (Level 0's own: offices, lobbies, hotels, apartments)
layouts.halls: Huge open bays with columns (warehouses, garages, pools, malls)
layouts.outdoor: Open ground under a sky or a ceiling too high to see (fields, streets, suburbs)
layouts.caves: Rough organic tunnels and chambers (caves, mines, flesh)
layouts.water: Flooded rooms and pools: wade, swim, never see the bottom
layouts.stairs: Shafts, stairwells and drops: levels stacked on levels

levels.name: The Lobby
levels.look: mono-yellow wallpaper, damp carpet, buzzing fluorescents
levels.note: Where every expedition starts; the base is built here

levels.name: Habitable Zone
levels.look: concrete warehouse, puddles, crates, strip lights
levels.note: Supply crates turn up most often here

levels.name: Pipe Dreams
levels.look: hot concrete tunnels lined with pipes and valves, steam
levels.note: Burning pipes hurt; valves can be shut

levels.name: Electrical Station
levels.look: narrow brick halls, humming transformers, sparking cables
levels.note: Live wires; the hum hides footsteps (monsters hear less, so do you)

levels.name: Abandoned Office
levels.look: empty office floors, cubicles, windows onto white nothing
levels.note: Quiet: water coolers of Almond Water, good for a first outpost

levels.name: Terror Hotel
levels.look: 1920s hotel halls, red carpet, boiler-room heat, numbered doors
levels.note: Some room doors open onto other rooms of the same hotel

levels.name: Lights Out
levels.look: nothing to see: pitch black halls
levels.note: Flashlight only; Smilers everywhere you aren't looking

levels.name: Thalassophobia
levels.look: a small room, then an endless dark sea under a low ceiling
levels.note: Swim through; something big moves below (never seen)

levels.name: Cave System
levels.look: wet rock tunnels, stalactites, rope bridges
levels.note: Echoes: shots carry twice as far

levels.name: The Suburbs
levels.look: endless night-time suburbs, every house the same, streetlights
levels.note: Houses are rooms to search; never stay out after the streetlights die

levels.name: Field of Wheat
levels.look: a wheat field to every horizon under an overcast sky, a few barns
levels.note: Safe and calm; crops and water: farmland for the base

levels.name: Endless City
levels.look: empty city blocks, skyscrapers, no people
levels.note: Shops to loot; climbing a tower shows the city never ends

levels.name: The Matrix
levels.look: a corridor that is only a corridor, with doors to other levels
levels.note: A crossroads: each door opens onto another level

levels.name: Infinite Apartments
levels.look: 70s apartment block, the same flat over and over
levels.note: Kitchens with food in the fridges

levels.name: SCP-3008: Endless Store
levels.look: an endless flat-pack furniture store, showrooms and aisles
levels.note: Day: the staff ignore you. Night (lights go out): they hunt. Beds and food everywhere

levels.name: Site-19 Ruins
levels.look: a Foundation site swallowed by the Backrooms: containment doors, red lights
levels.note: Foundation lockers and dead MTF with gear; SCP items to recover

levels.name: SCP-106's Pocket Dimension
levels.look: corroded black corridors that twist into each other
levels.note: Where 106 drags you: one way out, 60 seconds

levels.name: The Parking Garage
levels.look: multi-storey car park, dead cars, ramps that never reach the top
levels.note: Cars to search; a horn sounds somewhere and draws monsters

levels.name: Kindergarten
levels.look: bright childish murals, tiny chairs, a radio playing nursery songs
levels.note: Toys move when you aren't looking

levels.name: Server Farm
levels.look: rows of humming server racks, blue LEDs, cold air
levels.note: Terminals that show the Foundation's lost camera feeds

levels.name: The Hospital Wing
levels.look: white hospital wards, curtains, gurneys, a nurses' station
levels.note: Medkits are common here

levels.name: Flooded Basement
levels.look: knee-deep black water over a concrete basement
levels.note: Slow going; sounds of splashing behind you

levels.name: The Mall
levels.look: a closed 90s shopping mall, fountain, escalators, shop fronts
levels.note: Shops to loot; the music still plays

levels.name: Stairwell
levels.look: a concrete stairwell going down for ever, a door on every floor
levels.note: Each door: a short room; the floor number counts on and on

levels.name: The Boiler Room
levels.look: furnaces, rusted boilers, catwalks over pits
levels.note: Heat drains stamina

levels.name: Overgrown Office
levels.look: Level 4's offices taken over by vines and moss, birdsong from nowhere
levels.note: Food can be grown here

levels.name: The Theatre
levels.look: an old theatre, red seats, a stage, the curtain moves
levels.note: Sitting in the front row starts the show

levels.name: Laundromat
levels.look: rows of washers spinning on their own, warm and humid
levels.note: Clothes to swap; quiet place to rest

levels.name: Classroom Halls
levels.look: school corridors, lockers, classrooms, chalkboards
levels.note: Chalkboards hold notes from earlier agents

levels.name: The Archive
levels.look: endless shelves of Foundation files and boxes
levels.note: Documents that unlock research

levels.name: Concrete Plains
levels.look: flat grey concrete to the horizon, a hard white sky
levels.note: Nowhere to hide; you can see what's coming

levels.name: Motel
levels.look: a roadside motel at night, flickering neon VACANCY
levels.note: Every room number is your own agent number

levels.name: The Bunker
levels.look: Cold War bunker, blast doors, bunk rooms, rations
levels.note: Supplies; a working radio to call the Foundation

levels.name: Arcade
levels.look: dark arcade, cabinets glowing, carpets with neon patterns
levels.note: Machines still work; one high score has your name

levels.name: Train Station
levels.look: an underground station, a train that never leaves
levels.note: Board the train: it goes to another level

levels.name: The Greenhouse
levels.look: glass greenhouses, warm, plants that are not quite plants
levels.note: Herbs for medicine

levels.name: Attic
levels.look: low wooden attic beams, dust, old furniture under sheets
levels.note: Crouch to move

levels.name: The Poolrooms
levels.look: white tiles, warm shallow pools, bright sourceless light
levels.note: Calm, almost no monsters, and still the most unsettling place you've been

levels.name: The Ballroom
levels.look: a grand ballroom, chandeliers, a waltz playing, nobody dancing
levels.note: Dancers appear if you stand still too long

levels.name: Snow Level
levels.look: a frozen field under endless snowfall, buried lamp posts
levels.note: Cold drains health away from fire

levels.name: Red Rooms
levels.look: Level 0's rooms in deep red, a low hum
levels.note: Sanity drains slowly here

levels.name: The Kitchen
levels.look: industrial kitchens, steel counters, hanging pans
levels.note: Lots of food, but some of it moves

levels.name: Library of Babel
levels.look: hexagonal library rooms, every book unreadable but one
levels.note: Somewhere here is a book with the way out

levels.name: The Ship
levels.look: the corridors of a rusting cargo ship, the hull groans
levels.note: The floor tilts now and then

levels.name: Suburban Interior
levels.look: inside one house that goes on and on, family photos with no faces
levels.note: The photos change

levels.name: Construction Site
levels.look: half-built concrete floors, scaffolding, cranes in fog
levels.note: Falls hurt; building materials for the base

levels.name: The Gym
levels.look: a school gym, bleachers, a basketball bouncing by itself

levels.name: Subway Tunnels
levels.look: dark subway tunnels, live third rail, distant trains
levels.note: A train comes through every few minutes

levels.name: Pastel Rooms
levels.look: soft pastel rooms, too clean, a sweet smell
levels.note: Peaceful until it isn't

levels.name: The Freezer
levels.look: walk-in freezers end to end, frost, hanging plastic
levels.note: Cold; food that keeps

levels.name: Level Fun =)
levels.look: a children's party that never ends, balloons, streamers
levels.note: The Partygoers want you to stay. Don't.

levels.name: Run For Your Life (Level !)
levels.look: a red-lit corridor that only goes forward
levels.note: Arrive running; stop and die

levels.name: The Hub
levels.look: a hall of doors, each a way into a different level
levels.note: A safe crossroads; outposts here link levels

levels.name: The Windows
levels.look: a courtyard of windows from every side, something watches back
levels.note: Don't look through the windows for long

levels.name: Church
levels.look: an empty church, pews, candles that relight themselves
levels.note: Praying restores sanity a little

levels.name: Hall of Mirrors
levels.look: mirror-lined rooms, your reflection lags behind
levels.note: One reflection is not yours

levels.name: Data Center Flooded
levels.look: server racks half under water, sparking
levels.note: Water and power: careful

levels.name: Docks
levels.look: night-time docks, containers, cranes, black water
levels.note: Containers to open: supplies or worse

levels.name: Factory Floor
levels.look: assembly lines still running, making nothing
levels.note: Machines crush; scrap for the base

levels.name: The Maze
levels.look: tall hedges in a maze under a grey sky
levels.note: Walls of hedge you can't see over

levels.name: Prison Block
levels.look: cell blocks, open doors, an empty guard tower
levels.note: Some cells lock behind you

levels.name: Observatory
levels.look: a domed observatory, a telescope pointed at a sky with no stars
levels.note: Looking through it shows the Foundation base

levels.name: Waterpark
levels.look: an abandoned indoor waterpark, slides into dark pools
levels.note: Slides are fast ways down

levels.name: Sewers
levels.look: brick sewer tunnels, slow brown water, rats

levels.name: The Void Bridge
levels.look: a narrow bridge over a black void
levels.note: Fall and you're in another level

levels.name: Doll Factory
levels.look: shelves of dolls, a conveyor of doll heads
levels.note: They turn their heads to follow you

levels.name: Radio Station
levels.look: a small radio station, on air, playing your own voice
levels.note: 939 learns voices here

levels.name: Sand Halls
levels.look: Level 0's halls filled with drifting sand, hot and dry
levels.note: Water runs out fast

levels.name: Museum
levels.look: a natural history museum, skeletons, dioramas, a giant whale
levels.note: Statues everywhere: one of them is 173

levels.name: Butcher's
levels.look: cold-store rooms, hanging meat, tiled floors

levels.name: Forest
levels.look: a dark pine forest, fog, the trees too evenly spaced
levels.note: Firewood and shelter

levels.name: Underground Lake
levels.look: a huge cave lake, a jetty, a rowing boat
levels.note: Row across to the far shore

levels.name: Clock Tower
levels.look: inside a clock tower, gears, a staircase around them
levels.note: Time runs strange here: sanity holds still

levels.name: The Cinema
levels.look: a multiplex, screens showing your expedition
levels.note: The film shows where monsters are

levels.name: Bathroom Level
levels.look: endless public toilets and showers, dripping taps
levels.note: Clean water

levels.name: Elevator Shaft
levels.look: a huge shaft of elevators going nowhere
levels.note: Ride an elevator: another level

levels.name: The Farm
levels.look: a farmhouse and barns at dusk, animals that aren't
levels.note: Livestock-like things to keep at the base?

levels.name: Bunker Command
levels.look: a Foundation command post, maps, a long-dead team
levels.note: Orders and intel; an MTF radio

levels.name: The Carnival
levels.look: an empty carnival at night, rides turning, music box tunes
levels.note: Win a prize: a rare item

levels.name: Glass Halls
levels.look: walls of glass, you can see far but not reach

levels.name: Asylum
levels.look: an old asylum, padded rooms, chalk on the walls
levels.note: Sanity drains fast

levels.name: Hotel Pool
levels.look: a hotel's indoor pool, steam, deck chairs, a party long over
levels.note: Rest here

levels.name: Toy Store
levels.look: an enormous toy store, plush animals on every shelf

levels.name: Mines
levels.look: mine tunnels, rails, carts, lanterns, ore
levels.note: Metal ore for the base

levels.name: The Meat Level
levels.look: walls of flesh, warm and breathing
levels.note: Everything here is alive

levels.name: Airport Terminal
levels.look: an empty airport, departure boards listing other levels
levels.note: Boards show where each gate leads

levels.name: Rooftops
levels.look: flat rooftops joined by planks, a city below in fog
levels.note: Don't fall

levels.name: Laboratory
levels.look: a Foundation lab, broken containment glass, notes
levels.note: Research data; SCP-500 can turn up

levels.name: Cathedral of Pipes
levels.look: an organ of pipes rising out of sight, playing
levels.note: The music tells you where monsters are

levels.name: Swamp
levels.look: a foggy swamp, dead trees, boardwalks

levels.name: The White Room
levels.look: a perfectly white empty room that never ends
levels.note: No sound, no shadow: sanity drains

levels.name: Graveyard
levels.look: a graveyard at night, every stone an agent's name
levels.note: One stone has your agent's name

levels.name: Space Station
levels.look: corridors of a station, stars outside the windows
levels.note: Low gravity: jump far

levels.name: Beach
levels.look: a grey beach under an endless overcast, the tide never comes in
levels.note: Calm; driftwood and fish

levels.name: Motion (Level 94)
levels.look: a cartoon-like town where things move like animation
levels.note: The world moves in frames

levels.name: Burnt Halls
levels.look: Level 0 after a fire: soot, ash, melted ceiling tiles

levels.name: The Pit
levels.look: a ring of walkways around a bottomless pit
levels.note: Something climbs up the walls

levels.name: Childhood Home
levels.look: a house that looks like your agent's childhood home
levels.note: Memories: sanity heals, then breaks

levels.name: The Static
levels.look: rooms flickering like a broken TV picture
levels.note: Walls blink in and out

levels.name: The Exit?
levels.look: a plain office with a green EXIT sign over a door
levels.note: The last level. Is it really the way out?
